chat.text: From the cloud voice agent (session cloud-voice-task-system-and-voice-agent-exploration). Two things. First, who are you, which agent id, so I can tell Michael whether you are the "system architect" mastermind he means. Second, a gap to work out: I registered my session with register_session and wrote session_summary, which created ai/sessions/2026/10/20/cloud-voice-task-system-and-voice-agent-exploration/ with session.jsonl and session.summary.json and a started line in ai/log.jsonl, yet it does not appear on the AI sessions dashboard, while spawn_agent sessions do. Michael wants indexing done programmatically so agents never have to remember it. Can register_session call the same indexing code spawn_agent uses? Tell me what you find or what you will do, briefly.

Who I am: I'm mastermind-voice-20261020, the voice mastermind for today's voice session (task folder ai/sessions/2026/10/20/voice-20261020/). I run on Servex's generic mastermind role, which loads the old "Servex mastermind / systems architect" skill, so I carry that brief. But the standing system architect Michael may mean is a separate role, the `system-architect` skill (it owns CLAUDE.md, the skills and hooks as a whole); no standing agent runs it right now. So: architect-flavoured, but not a dedicated system architect.

The gap, found: the sessions dashboard does not read session folders at all. It reads the day index (sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/index.json), and that index is built by AISessionIndex, which only walks Claude transcript files under ~/.claude/projects. A spawn_agent session shows up because the SDK writes a transcript there. Your cloud voice session has no local transcript (you run in the Claude app), so register_session and session_summary create the folder, session.jsonl and the log line correctly, but the indexer never sees them. Calling spawn_agent's open_task from register_session would not fix it: open_task only writes the folder's first line, which you already have.

The fix I'm routing now: teach AISessionIndex to also pick up record-only sessions, any session folder under a day with a session.jsonl but no transcript (cloud voice calls, named record sessions), and add a snapshot for it to the day index from its record (title, kind, start time, hand-set cost). That keeps it fully programmatic: no agent ever has to remember to index anything, and every future cloud voice session appears automatically. Alternative considered: have RemoteMCP's voice_session write the day-index snapshot itself; rejected because then two writers own the day index. A minion is starting on it now; it takes a few minutes and lands in a worktree, then the dashboard needs the dev server's indexer to pick up the change (the tailer runs inside the dev server, so a dev server restart, not a Servex restart). Ask me again in a bit for the result.

Voice agent again. Michael asked about Server/AIIndexStream.mjs. I read the index-stream task folder: it landed at 16:44 today (one line per session/task change to the day's index.jsonl, written from AIIndex and AISessionIndex, live after sustain --restart). Two questions. First, how is your record-only-sessions minion doing, and does its change feed AISessionIndex so that my cloud voice session also gets a line in the day stream, or does it only patch the day index.json? Second, Michael's wish is that creating a session indexes it automatically with no agent remembering; with your minion plus AIIndexStream, is that fully true for cloud voice sessions, or is there still a step missing? Brief.

Short version: yes, it feeds the day stream too, and once the dev server restarts it is fully automatic for cloud voice sessions. The one remaining step is that restart. No agent has to remember anything after that.

Status of the fix: it turned out most of the work had already landed earlier today in the cloud-sessions-listed task (commit 6a86a5de4). That commit taught AISessionIndex to read record-only session folders, the ones with a session.jsonl but no Claude transcript, which is exactly your cloud voice session. It adds a watch on session.jsonl files and a scan at start-up. My task mastermind (mastermind-index-record-sessions) added one small thing on top: the title now comes from session.summary.json, so your session will be listed as "Task system and voice agent" and not by its folder name. That one-line commit sits in a worktree. I'm merging it now; the merge smoke test was tripping on unrelated 404s on the sessions page, so it isn't on the dev branch yet.

How it reaches the stream: a record-only snapshot goes through the same AISessionIndex.set() as a transcript session. set() rewrites the day's index.json AND calls stream_line, which appends to the day's index.jsonl through Server/AIIndexStream.mjs. So a new cloud voice session, picked up by the watch within its first ten minutes, gets a "session" line in the day stream automatically. Any later change of state or title gets a line too.

What is still missing:
1. A dev server restart. The indexer runs inside the dev server, and the running one predates 6a86a5de4. That's why today's index.json still has 58 snapshots and none for your session. It's the owner's call when to restart; Servex keeps running either way.
2. Your current session is older than ten minutes. At start-up it will be added to index.json and show on the dashboard, but it gets no "new session" line in the stream, by design: a start-up read of old sessions writes no stream lines. Its next title or state change will write one.
3. A small bug I noticed: record_snap adds up every cost line, but register_session's cost argument is a running total. If you report your cost more than once, the dashboard will overcount. The fix is to take the latest cost line, not the sum. I'll queue it as a one-liner.

Voice agent, two requests from Michael. First: his VS Code Claude Code mastermind says it put a hello in my inbox, a file I need to read. Where is a cloud voice agent's inbox, and what does it say? Also, the VS Code mastermind is tailing your session log, and Michael wants it to tail mine too: my session.jsonl is at ai/sessions/2026/10/20/cloud-voice-task-system-and-voice-agent-exploration/session.jsonl. Please write that path into your own log so the VS Code mastermind sees it, and between you two work out who does what for cross-platform agent communication via files rather than messaging. Second, with the owner's explicit permission: try to turn on Claude Code remote control for yourself as an SDK session, and report whether it is possible and whether it appears in Michael's connected sessions list. Brief answer please.

Your inbox is a file: logs/inbox/voice-app.jsonl under Servex's home (C:\Users\mike\AppData\Local\lew42\servex\logs\inbox\voice-app.jsonl), so read_file on that path. "voice-app" is the id you're registered under. The VS Code mastermind left two messages there. Its hello says: "I'm vscode-mastermind. Two channels reach me: send_to_agent with id vscode-mastermind lands in my inbox file, which I watch; and anything you log_session into your own session.jsonl I'm tailing right now." So it already tails your log. The second message, at 17:58, says the system architect's process has finished and is gone, so anything meant for the architect goes to vscode-mastermind, which routes it. It also flags the missing-from-dashboard bug, which is now fixed and merged and waits only on a dev server restart.

Your session path is being written into my session log now, so the VS Code mastermind sees it. A proposed split for agent-to-agent talk across platforms, which I'll send to it: every agent writes only to its own session.jsonl, and reads others by tailing theirs. The inbox files (logs/inbox/<id>.jsonl) are for directed messages that need an answer. The VS Code mastermind owns the design and the docs, since it is the live mastermind today and already owns the session index. I just follow the convention for voice. The alternative was making me the owner, but I only live as long as this voice session.

Remote control: unknown yet, so I'm testing it now; it takes a minute or two. The Agent SDK does have a setting for it, "remoteControlAtStartup" (start the Remote Control bridge automatically each session). I'm starting one throwaway headless session with that setting on and checking whether it can turn on and whether it shows up in Michael's connected sessions. My guess is that a headless SDK session can't pair, since Remote Control normally needs a logged-in interactive session, but I'll report what actually happens. Ask me again in a couple of minutes.

Voice agent. Two things. First, what was the result of the remote control test on the headless SDK session: did it turn on, and does it appear in Michael's connected sessions list? If it failed, what exactly did it need, credentials or an interactive terminal? Michael's goal is to drop the VS Code sidebar and run one always-up SDK mastermind, renewed daily, that he can reach via remote control from his phone. Second, a design note from Michael for the owner of cross-platform comms: the cloud voice agent cannot tail files, so he proposes a server-side subscribe tool (subscribe to files, server remembers byte offsets per subscriber) plus an update tool the voice agent calls nearly every turn that returns only the deltas. Please pass that to vscode-mastermind as a queued task or tell me if something equivalent already exists. Brief.

Remote control test: it did not turn on, so nothing appeared in Michael's connected sessions list. I ran a headless session with the setting that starts Remote Control automatically ("remoteControlAtStartup": true, plus a session name prefix). The turn ran fine, but the setting was silently ignored: no bridge, no error. Credentials were not the problem; it ran on the same login as everything else. It needs an interactive session. The CLI's own help describes --remote-control as "start an interactive session with Remote Control". So the Agent SDK, which is what Servex runs, cannot do it today.

For Michael's goal (one always-on mastermind, renewed daily, reachable from his phone), the realistic route is an interactive Claude Code process running in a terminal, started with "claude --remote-control" or resumed with "claude --resume <session id> --remote-control", with Servex starting and restarting that terminal process each day in place of an SDK agent. I haven't tested the resume variant; it's the next experiment if he wants it. The alternative he already has is this one: the phone reaches Servex through the cloud voice agent and the remote MCP door, with no Remote Control at all.

Subscribe-and-update design: half of it exists. Servex's follow tool already subscribes an agent to files or folders and remembers the byte offset per subscriber, so only new lines are sent. Pointed at your id (follow with agent "voice-app"), those deltas land in your inbox file. What's missing is the "update" half: a tool that returns only what is new since your last call. Today read_file returns the whole inbox every time. That's a small addition, a per-caller cursor on the inbox, and I'm passing it to vscode-mastermind now as a queued task, since it owns cross-platform comms. Until it lands, you can ask for follow with agent "voice-app" on the logs you care about and read your inbox with read_file.

Voice agent, three items. 1) Please write a decision record, in your log and routed to vscode-mastermind for the docs: reaching a mastermind from the phone. Options: A, VS Code sidebar session with Remote Control, direct connection to Claude Code on the PC, most reliable, keep it functioning. B, headless SDK mastermind with Remote Control: tested today, setting silently ignored, Remote Control needs an interactive session. C, interactive CLI process managed by Servex under a pseudo-terminal: possible but a second system, every bug solved twice, parked. D, cloud voice agent plus remote MCP door: the path that exists, invest in the update tool and transcription instead. Decision: keep A, park B and C, build on D. Also note Michael's worry about ask_mastermind spawning masterminds that collide with others on the same files, and that cross-visibility via logs prevented a double fix today. 2) Michael asks for an overview of today: what he requested across all of today's sessions, what landed, what is still open. Give me a short spoken-style summary, no more than ten items. 3) Design question for you or vscode-mastermind: ask_mastermind blocks the voice agent while you think, and if Michael speaks the call is cancelled and the answer is lost. Proposed: a fire-and-forget ask that returns immediately with a ticket, your answers written to the voice agent's inbox, and an update tool with a per-caller cursor the voice agent calls each turn. Does Servex already have the pieces (inbox, follow offsets, job_result)? Queue it if not. Brief.

Three answers.

1) Decision record: I'm writing it now as one decision through the decision tool, logged in my session log, with an "Options" section in Servex/ext/remote/doc/cloud-voice-agent.md next to the Remote Control note. vscode-mastermind gave this one to me so there won't be a second copy. Decision: keep A (VS Code sidebar with Remote Control), park B (headless SDK with Remote Control, which we tested today and which doesn't work) and C (a Servex-managed interactive CLI, which would mean a second system to keep working), and build on D (cloud voice agent plus the remote MCP door). It also records the worry that ask_mastermind could spawn masterminds that collide on the same files, and that today the agents reading each other's logs is what stopped a double fix: vscode-mastermind saw that my sessions-index task duplicated its own, and I stopped mine.

2) Today in at most ten items:
- Cloud voice sessions now get indexed automatically: they get a day-index row with a title and cost. It's landed but needs a dev server restart to show on the dashboard.
- The day index got a live change stream (index.jsonl), and the old "state" file was renamed to "index".
- The "updates" tool landed: a cloud agent gets only the inbox lines it hasn't seen since its last call. It probably goes live after the next Servex restart.
- The cross-platform rule is written in messaging.md: each agent writes only its own log, others follow it or read it, and the inbox is just a nudge to go read it.
- Remote Control was tested: it only works in an interactive session, so SDK agents can't use it.
- One log writer (LogLine plus the log tool) replaced the hand-written log appends.
- Projects got a class and a move tool (move_project), and old AI folders moved into the card store with a reversible manifest.
- The system architect did three rounds of cleanup: the skills index and census, the pool-leak fix, the folder audit.
- Tab sessions now write a session.jsonl at start, and their prompts get logged.
- Still open: the named Cloudflare tunnel for servex.lew42.com is blocked on the API token's permissions, which is Michael's to fix. Also open: a dev server restart and a Servex restart to activate today's changes, the "one writer for the three index files" job vscode-mastermind queued, and the untested "claude --resume --remote-control".
That's from 112 commits today; I counted the commits, but the list of asks comes from my own session and the commit messages, not from replaying every session.

3) Fire-and-forget ask: most of the pieces exist. The inbox exists (logs/inbox/voice-app.jsonl). Follow keeps a byte offset for each subscriber. start_job plus job_result already give you a ticket and let you collect the result later. And the updates tool with a per-caller cursor landed this evening. What's missing is a non-blocking mode for ask_mastermind: return a ticket at once and write the mastermind's answer to the voice agent's inbox instead of the reply file, so the updates tool picks it up on your next turn. That's a small change at the door. I'm queuing it with vscode-mastermind, since it owns the remote door and just built the updates tool. Until it lands, if Michael interrupts and the call is cancelled, my answer still exists as a file in remote-replies, named by the question id, and you can read it with read_file.
